goal: Infer reusable per-part periodic motion from 36 noisy AI observations, resample it to an 8-frame loop, and render approved canonical freeform parts with phase-dependent shape, projection, shading, occlusion, and z-order.

final_target.motion_source: robust periodic model inferred from observation frames

verified.walk_compiler: 5 authored directions x 8 frames -> 8 directions x 8 frames with Godot resources

full_test_suite.note: Use a fresh writable project-local --basetemp on Windows.

prototype_only.platekit/character/partize.py: Coarse visible-pixel ownership seed; not semantic rig-ready segmentation and no hidden joint overlap.
prototype_only.platekit/character/rig.py: Ratio/silhouette anchor estimates; no full temporal anatomical identity or periodic phase model.
prototype_only.platekit/character/overlay.py: Failed/research outfit overlay and rebuild experiments; not a production garment-transfer implementation.

not_implemented: fine freeform anatomical part masks and SDFs
non_negotiable: A part is a freeform alpha mask or SDF, never a rectangular crop.
Translation and rotation alone are insufficient for body and fitted-cloth motion.
Each body/fitted part needs phase-dependent silhouette deformation and shading information.
Projected limb length and width may change with gait phase and foreshortening.
Anatomical left/right identity must persist through screen-space crossing.
Canonical albedo/texture must be separated from observed phase-dependent shading.
Rigid, fitted, and loose parts use different transform models.
Cross-view transfer is rejected; mirroring is only within one view family.
Unknown occluded pixels remain unknown until authored or approved.
Background, Dig, Room, Light, and existing Walk behavior must remain unchanged.

next_milestone.name: front-36 temporal freeform observation model
deliverables: fine part masks/SDFs with confidence and unknown regions
per-part translation, rotation, projected scale, cage/SDF delta, shading, z-order, and occlusion observations
skeleton, freeform-morph, and shading contact sheets
